techniques.evidence: src/features/plugins/fleet/__tests__/SkillLibraryDrawer.test.tsx:123-124 says 'The carriage return is what submits it' and asserts '/compact'+CR as a single writeInput payload; the technique requires paste-this and press-this-key as separate verbs, and the backend has to split them again at src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/commands.rs:199

src/features/plugins/fleet/__tests__/FleetTerminalOverlay.test.tsx:11 stubs the tiles so xterm never loads; the ladder is tested in files outside this context (fleetTerminalAttachOrder.test.ts, FleetTerminalOverlayKeepAlive.test.tsx)

src/features/plugins/fleet/__tests__/fleetAttention.test.ts:26 pins attention to the Rust hook-derived stateReason verdict, not to screen scraping; the technique says not to build a screen classifier when the occupant emits lifecycle hooks

pairs.registryProposal: Ownership gap, not a corpus gap: src/features/plugins/fleet/__tests__/FleetBroadcastPayload.test.tsx belongs to no context in context-map.json, and it is the file that pins the live keystroke-injection deviation as expected behaviour (~line 115 expects a raw 'draft\nonly' payload with no paste framing). Several other fleet terminal tests (fleetTerminalAttachOrder, FleetTerminalOverlayKeepAlive, FleetTerminalPaneLiveness) also look unassigned to this context, so this pair is judged on a context that omits most of the fleet terminal tests. A rescan should assign them to plugins-fleet-tests or fleet-terminal-manager.
